title: Capstone: Entity-Component-System Engine
hints: A small template gives each component a number: `template <typename C> constexpr std::size_t indexOf();` with specialisations returning 0, 1 and 2. That number picks the vector and the bit.
`std::tuple<std::vector<Position>, std::vector<Velocity>, std::vector<Health>> m_storage;` and `std::get<std::vector<C>>(m_storage)` picks the right vector from the type alone.
Write `each<A, B>` last: loop over all entity ids, skip those whose bitset lacks either bit, and call `f(get<A>(e), get<B>(e))`.
requirements: `World` stores each component type in its own `std::vector`, indexed by entity id, plus a `std::bitset<3>` per entity saying which components it has
`each<A, B>(f)` that calls `f` for every entity that has both components
A simulation of 1,000 moving particles that lose health and are removed when it reaches 0
stretch: `World<Cs...>` for any list of components with a variadic template, and a speed comparison with a `std::vector<std::unique_ptr<GameObject>>` version.
